summary: Raila Amolo Odinga is a veteran Kenyan political leader, former Prime Minister (2008–2013), and leader of the Azimio La Umoja One Kenya Coalition Party. A central figure in Kenya's multi-party democracy movement and five-time presidential candidate, Odinga's career has combined anti-authoritarian advocacy with parliamentary inquiries into state enterprise privatizations and coalition governance.
introduction: Raila Amolo Odinga (born 7 January 1945) has been a dominant force in Kenyan politics for more than three decades. Following the disputed 2007 presidential elections and subsequent National Accord, Odinga served as Kenya's Prime Minister coordinating executive functions. During his tenure, his office faced intense scrutiny over the World Bank-financed Kazi Kwa Vijana (KKV) youth employment initiative, where forensic audits raised documentation discrepancies before oversight bodies cleared him of personal malfeasance. Other historical inquiries include the 2003 privatization review of the Kisumu Molasses Plant acquired by Spectre International Ltd. In 2024, Odinga negotiated a political détente with President Ruto, securing Kenyan state backing for his candidacy for African Union Commission (AUC) Chairperson.
